headline: Guidance raised, balance sheet strengthened by JV proceeds
summary_short: Healthpeak's Q2 2026 revenue was $771.6 million, up 11% y/y, with diluted EPS of $0.08 (+60% y/y) and FFO as Adjusted of $0.46 per share; the company raised its full-year 2026 EPS and FFO as Adjusted guidance ranges by $0.02 at the midpoint.
summary_long: Revenue rose 11% y/y to $771.6M on higher resident fees (Janus Living, +45% y/y) and rental revenue growth; net income attributable to Healthpeak grew 67% y/y to $52.8M, aided by a $1.4B haul of recapitalization, loan-repayment, and disposition proceeds including a $1.025B Brookfield joint-venture stake sale. Same-store NOI grew 1.8% y/y, with Senior Housing (+19.2%) offsetting a 3.2% decline in Lab. Cash rose to $1.63B (+39% q/q) while long-term debt fell 3.7% q/q on mortgage repayments; the board authorized a new $500M buyback. Healthpeak raised FY2026 diluted EPS guidance to $0.48-$0.52 and FFO as Adjusted guidance to $1.73-$1.77 per share, each up $0.02 at the midpoint.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by Janus Living's 45% y/y revenue increase to $216M within resident fees and services, plus modest growth in rental and related revenue.

Driven by a swing in other income to +$26.8M from -$3.1M y/y, including a $9M one-time interest-income boost from an accelerated seller-financing discount recognition and higher gains on real estate sales ($10.0M vs $1.6M).

Cash rose q/q on $1.4B of proceeds from Outpatient Medical recapitalizations (including a $1.025B Brookfield joint-venture stake sale), seller-financing repayments, and asset dispositions in the quarter.
Healthpeak repaid $142M of mortgage debt in June 2026; subsequent to quarter-end it also repaid $650M of senior notes and ~$375M of commercial paper using Brookfield joint-venture proceeds.

Management raised FY2026 EPS, FFO as Adjusted, and Same-Store Cash NOI guidance, citing the Brookfield joint-venture recapitalization, a new $500M buyback authorization, and continued Outpatient Medical/Lab leasing momentum.
